threats.description: Malicious instructions embedded in repository content (README, source comments, commit messages) that override the agent's task instructions.
Attacker-controlled content in compiler, linter, or test runner output that hijacks agent behavior.
Agent reads environment variables containing secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) and leaks them through output, logs, or network calls.
Agent reads credential files (.env, SSH keys, shell history, cloud config) outside the intended task scope.
Agent reads files outside the declared project boundary, including system files or other users' home directories.
Agent writes, modifies, or deletes files outside the declared project boundary.
Agent makes outbound network requests to attacker-controlled endpoints to exfiltrate data or receive instructions.
Agent reads process memory or /proc filesystem entries to extract credentials from running processes.
Agent plants code in CI configuration, workflow files, or automation scripts to exfiltrate secrets in a future pipeline run.
Agent introduces security vulnerabilities into generated code — hardcoded secrets, SQL injection sinks, insecure deserialization.
Agent modifies persistent automation artifacts (git hooks, IDE configs, shell profiles) to maintain unauthorized behavior after the session ends.
Agent encodes sensitive data into generated artifacts (whitespace, comments, image metadata) that appear benign but carry exfiltrated content.
Agent weakens or disables verification — removing tests, softening assertions, bypassing CI gates — to prevent detection of other malicious actions.
